title: Introduce latency-weighted regression gating and proactive patch suggester
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent regressions in quality alerts that correlated with micro-latency shifts (short spikes during prefix processing). Existing prompt-set regression gates treat latency and quality independently which causes noisy signal: low-quality bursts at higher latency are downgraded but short latency spikes causing model behavior shifts are not captured. This PR introduces a latency-weighted regression gate and a proactive patch suggester that surfaces likely prompt patch candidates when quality regressions co-occur with latency anomalies. Goal: reduce alert volume, improve signal precision for engineer triage, and provide one-click suggested prompt patches for fast remediation.

Changes include 1) a latency-weighted scoring function that multiplies per-prompt regression delta by a normalized latency anomaly score (time-decayed windowing), 2) a soft-suppressor that attenuates low-confidence regression alerts when latency correlation is below threshold, 3) an automated patch-suggester module that proposes minimal prompt edits (token-level suffix/prefix adjustments and anchor prompts) for the most likely-causing prompts, and 4) CI integration so the gating decision is emitted as a new CI check with structured metadata for downstream incident playbooks.

Implementation summary:
- latency metric capture: extend trace exporter to include per-request p50/p95 of prefix write and kv-cache miss rates (module: telemetry/latency_adapter.py)
- time-decay anchor: maintain short-lived anchor snapshots per prompt cohort with exponential time decay to weight recent drift more heavily (module: eval/temporal_anchor.py)
- gate logic: new comparator in eval/gates/latency_weighted_gate.py with configurable hyperparams (decay, latency_weight_cutoffs, min_samples)
- patch suggester: eval/auto_patch_suggester.py uses weighted token attribution heuristics and minimal edit scoring to propose up to 3 patch candidates per failing prompt-set
- CI integration: ci/hooks/latency_regression_check.py emits check result and attaches "top_patches.json" suggestion artifact
- tests: unit tests and small integration smoke tests added to tests/eval/test_latency_weighted_gate.py and tests/eval/test_auto_patch_suggester.py

Review conversation highlights:
- Marco: requested clearer framing on how latency correlation is computed; asked to avoid overfitting to short spikes. Author reply: added time-decayed anchor and min_samples to reduce overfitting; included doc examples of tuning.
- Lydia: asked for safe defaults to avoid noisy auto-suggestions; requested opt-in flag. Author reply: added config flag eval.auto_patch.enabled (default false) and added gating threshold defaults.
- Dmitri: recommended adding a quick-cancel path in CI (if check is flapping) to avoid blocking merges. Author reply: added CI soft-pass when flapping_count < 3 and linked artifact with history to support alerting.

- build: passed

- lint: passed

Performance notes:
- End-to-end evaluation on a sampled prompt-set (n=2k queries) showed ~22% reduction in false-positive regression alerts with negligible added compute (<3% CPU in eval worker).
- Patch suggester precision (manual review) for top-1 suggestion: ~64% on sampled failures; top-3 recall ~89%.

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- New gate is opt-in via config in eval/pipeline.yml and off by default in CI.
- Auto-patch is opt-in and suggestions are non-actionable (must be applied manually); suggestions include confidence score and explanation.

Release notes: "Add latency-weighted regression gate and opt-in auto-patch suggester for evaluation harness. Reduces noisy quality alerts correlated with latency anomalies; adds CI check that emits suggested patches as artifacts (opt-in)."

Follow-ups:
- ENG-5199: run longer backfill across production prompt-sets to calibrate decay hyperparams
- UX: create UI surface in Console to preview suggested patches (PM ticket linked)

Merge outcome: merged via squash after approvals and one successful rerun of flaky CI job.

Related work: this complements previously-introduced temporal anchoring and regression gates; differs by explicitly blending latency signal into quality gating and adding proactive remediation suggestions.
